summary.headline: Four season themes and one mission context behind the next match.
summary.note: Themes are hypotheses with evidence, not verdicts. Provider ratings are labelled and never an individual verdict.

caveats: Provider ratings are not position-adjusted and are not a fitba rating.
The rating sample is Premiership-only; starts and minutes include cup fixtures.
A family mean can hide a high-variance unit; the 25th percentile and spread matter.
The squad-page position-group rating is an equal-weighted season aggregate and mixes full-backs with centre-backs; this layer uses per-match starters.

themes.method: Minutes-weighted mean of provider match ratings for starters with an observed role. Goals and assists use the player's primary family so substitutes count.

scope.note: Provider ratings are Premiership-only and current-season. They are not position-adjusted; cross-family comparison is descriptive.

themes.read: Provider ratings put GK at the top (7.46) and W at the bottom (6.56). The CB family mean is 7.01, +0.05 against the squad mean. The data does not show a weak CB family overall; it shows dispersion and a shape effect. Ratings are provider match ratings, not a fitba rating and not position-adjusted.

caveats: Kick-off shape only; mid-game switches are not inferred.

themes.fan_question: What does three at the back cost?
themes.headline: Three at the back is a wing-back tax: the wide defenders start, the wide forwards do not.

implications.line: Full-backs / wing-backs: strengthen; medium urgency; market route permanent.
Wide forwards: strengthen; medium urgency; market route permanent.

themes.method: Group fixtures by kick-off centre-back count, then count observed wing-back, full-back and wide-forward starters, named bench rows and substitute minutes.
themes.read: There are 4 three-CB fixtures and 9 two-CB fixtures. Wing-backs start 2.0 per match in the three-CB set and 0.0 in the two-CB set; wide forwards start 0.0 vs 1.3. Three-CB games concede 1.25 goals per match vs 0.78, with 5.3 vs 4.2 saves per match where saves are available. This is an association in a small sample, not a causal claim.

themes.method: League match rows for goals, shots and points; provider goals joined to the squad's primary role family.
themes.read: The league season is 10-10 with 11 points. Forwards scored 6 of 10 goals (60%); the data shows where the goals come from and what the team concedes. It does not prove the forwards are "bailing out" the defence, and there is no xG or shot-quality model here.

themes.fan_question: Is the trading model working, or just a leaky boat?
themes.headline: The model is visible in the turnover; the sporting cost is an unsettled back line.
themes.method: Join the published era scorecard, 2026-27 recruitment/selection aggregates and the transfer register. No historical ratings exist.

metrics.commercial_context: Commercial growth and fanbase expansion are part of the public framing of the Cormack era. They are context only: the public football data cannot measure them, so they are not scored.

pillars.statement: Recruit players whose current output or potential is priced below their likely future value, give them minutes, and realise value when the offer and the sporting cost balance.
pillars.title: Buy low, develop, sell high

pillars.statement: A development-and-sale model needs a pathway: academy graduates and young signings have to get first-team minutes, not just squad numbers.
pillars.title: Develop and play young players

pillars.statement: Recruitment and selection should serve a recognisable way of playing. The record shows the observed shapes and match-stat proxies, and labels the tactical reading separately.
pillars.title: A defined style of play

pillars.statement: Look for under-appreciated players in poorer teams, undervalued Scottish players, and markets the domestic game overlooks. The record shows the source market, age, known fee and minutes; it does not yet score "undervalued" itself.
pillars.title: Undervalued players and overlooked markets

pillars.statement: A trading model accepts squad turnover and young-player variance in exchange for commercial and developmental upside. Cup runs are real achievements and a source of variance, not proof that the league model is working.
pillars.title: Squad turnover, league variance and cup runs

recruitment.note: Disclosed fees only. Undisclosed is never zero and is excluded from the totals. Age is shown only where a birth date is known.

valuation.note: Estimated net spend range from public/reported fees and a transparent model. The aggregate uses modelled midpoints with a 20% portfolio band on modelled gross flows, not the sum of every row's extremes. Free transfers count as zero fee; loan fees are excluded. Negative means income exceeds spend. Not an audited balance.

valuation.note: Estimated net spend range from public/reported fees and a transparent model. The aggregate uses modelled midpoints with a 20% portfolio band on modelled gross flows, not the sum of every row's extremes. Free transfers count as zero fee; loan fees are excluded. selection.note: Formation is the kick-off shape. Ages use the season roster or a known birth date; missing ages are excluded, not filled. Top-by-starts is not a claim that those players started together.
selection.tactical_note: Selection metrics are current-season and coverage-labelled. A young or newly assembled squad can produce volatile minutes; the page shows the distribution rather than a single average.

themes.read: The 2026-27 rebuild shows 15 arrivals and 25 departures, a median arrival age of 26, U21 minutes at 8% and 37 players used. That is the trading model visible in the squad: high turnover, young minutes and a changing back line. The data can show the trade-off; it cannot decide whether the club's risk appetite is right.
